title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #13

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part of the plant is usually flat, green and spread out to catch light? (1 mark)
   A. Stem
   B. Root
   C. Leaf
   D. Seed

2. Which sign of life do ALL living things eventually show? (1 mark)
   A. Flying
   B. Making seeds
   C. Dying
   D. Flowering

3. Which of these is a good way to care for plants at school? (1 mark)
   A. Pick all the flowers
   B. Water them when the soil is dry
   C. Throw litter on them
   D. Trample on flower beds

4. Which of these is a mammal? (1 mark)
   A. Frog
   B. Crocodile
   C. Cow
   D. Tilapia

5. Which of these is the best question to ask first when you sort an animal into vertebrate or invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Is it big?
   B. Does it have a backbone?
   C. Is it fast?
   D. Is it dangerous?

6. Which of these statements is true? (1 mark)
   A. All fish have a backbone
   B. All animals have six legs
   C. All animals can fly
   D. All small animals are insects

7. Which of these animals has an outside skeleton or hard covering and no backbone? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Crab
   C. Tilapia
   D. Hen

8. What should you do with a small animal after you observe it? (1 mark)
   A. Return it to where you found it
   B. Take it home in your pocket
   C. Squash it
   D. Give it to a friend

9. What is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with six legs
   B. An animal with a backbone
   C. An animal without bones
   D. An animal that lives in water only

10. Which of these is an insect? (1 mark)
   A. Snail
   B. Butterfly
   C. Crab
   D. Earthworm

11. Which of these is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Snake
   B. Goat
   C. Frog
   D. Earthworm

12. Which of these animals is a reptile? (1 mark)
   A. Lizard
   B. Butterfly
   C. Tilapia
   D. Hen

13. Why is a plan for a healthy digestive system useful? (1 mark)
   A. It cures all diseases at once
   B. It stops us feeling hungry
   C. It makes us grow overnight
   D. It reminds us to do the right things every day

14. Which of these is a good use of a school deworming day? (1 mark)
   A. Refuse to take them
   B. Give them to animals
   C. Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   D. Throw them away

15. Which of these can cause stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Brushing teeth
   B. Drinking clean water
   C. Washing hands
   D. Eating too fast or germs in dirty food

16. Another name for the gullet is (1 mark)
   A. Oesophagus
   B. Tongue
   C. Anus
   D. Rectum

17. What is bloating? (1 mark)
   A. A cut in the mouth
   B. Tiredness
   C. A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   D. Loose faeces

18. A cup can hold about (1 mark)
   A. 250 ml
   B. 2500 ml
   C. 25 litres
   D. 25 ml

19. Which of these is a gas? (1 mark)
   A. Water in a cup
   B. A wooden spoon
   C. The air in a balloon
   D. Flour

20. Why should each child use their own balloon for the balloon activity? (1 mark)
   A. To avoid spreading germs
   B. To make the balloon bigger
   C. To make it heavier
   D. To make it burst

21. A jug has 400 ml of water. Fatuma adds 250 ml. How much water is in the jug? (1 mark)
   A. 600 ml
   B. 150 ml
   C. 450 ml
   D. 650 ml

22. A kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same (1 mark)
   A. Mass
   B. Shape
   C. Colour
   D. Volume

23. Sand pours like a liquid. What state is each grain? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Steam
   C. Solid
   D. Liquid

24. Which of these is a tool for picking up waste safely? (1 mark)
   A. A towel
   B. Bare hands
   C. A rake
   D. Bare feet

25. Which reused water is safe for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Water that washed vegetables
   B. None of the used washing water
   C. Water that washed a car
   D. Water that washed clothes

26. Why should a rainwater tank be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To make it rain
   B. To make water heavier
   C. To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   D. To keep the water warm

27. Which of these is needed to harvest rainwater from a roof? (1 mark)
   A. A gutter and a tank
   B. A ladder only
   C. A fan
   D. A torch

28. Why should you keep drinking water in a clean covered container? (1 mark)
   A. To make it colder
   B. To make it salty
   C. To keep it safe from germs
   D. To make it hot

29. Which of these is a way of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving a tap running
   B. Fixing leaks
   C. Using a bucket
   D. Closing taps

30. A stone and a crumpled paper are dropped together. They land almost together because (1 mark)
   A. The paper is heavier
   B. Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   C. The stone is lighter
   D. There is no gravity

31. What effect does friction have on rubbing your hands? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them cold
   B. It makes them warm
   C. It makes them heavy
   D. It makes them wet

32. A pump pushing air into a tyre is an example of (1 mark)
   A. A force
   B. A shadow
   C. A colour
   D. A gas

33. Which surface gives the most friction? (1 mark)
   A. A smooth ice surface
   B. A polished tile
   C. A rough carpet
   D. An oiled floor

34. Which of these is a natural source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. The sun
   C. A bulb
   D. A candle

35. Which of these is opaque? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water
   B. Wood
   C. Clear plastic
   D. Clear glass

36. Which of these is an artificial way of lighting a house? (1 mark)
   A. Moonlight
   B. Windows
   C. Sun through the door
   D. Electric bulbs

37. Which of these gives artificial light by burning paraffin? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Star
   C. Paraffin lamp
   D. Lightning

38. Which of these is NOT a source of heat? (1 mark)
   A. A kettle
   B. The sun
   C. A burning log
   D. A cold stone in the shade

39. Which of these is a source of heat from burning? (1 mark)
   A. A ruler
   B. A book
   C. A cup
   D. Charcoal

40. What should you use to hold a hot cooking pot? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bag
   B. Bare hands
   C. Wet cloth
   D. Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name the two forces studied in this topic. (2 marks)

42. Describe how you would show that light travels in a straight line. (3 marks)

43. Describe five ways in which forces are used at home and on the farm. (5 marks)

44. Name two ways of lighting a house during the day. (2 marks)

45. Name three gases and say how each is useful. (3 marks)

46. Explain why a spider is not an insect. (3 marks)

47. Describe two properties of a liquid. (3 marks)

48. Group these into solid, liquid and gas: milk, chalk, oxygen, cooking oil, book, steam. (4 marks)

49. Give two safety rules when using an electric iron. (2 marks)

50. Give three examples of things that use electricity to make heat. (3 marks)

51. Name the three states of matter and give one example of each. (2 marks)

52. Describe how you can show that a liquid takes the shape of its container. (3 marks)

53. Suggest two ways to make toys or ornaments from waste and the materials needed. (4 marks)

54. Describe how to show that metal passes heat more easily than wood. (3 marks)

55. State two dangers of leaving waste in the environment. (2 marks)

56. Discuss how a family can light their home cheaply and safely. (5 marks)

57. Give two ways in which water is wasted at school. (2 marks)

58. Explain the importance of heat in daily life. (5 marks)

59. What happens in the large intestine? (2 marks)

60. Give two reasons why solids are useful in daily life. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Leaf
   The flat, green shape of a leaf helps it catch light.

2. C — Dying
   Every living thing dies one day, but not all fly, flower or make seeds.

3. B — Water them when the soil is dry
   Watering when dry helps plants live and grow.

4. C — Cow
   A cow has hair and feeds its calf on milk.

5. B — Does it have a backbone?
   The backbone decides the group.

6. A — All fish have a backbone
   Fish are vertebrates. Small animals may be spiders, worms or others.

7. B — Crab
   A crab has a hard outer shell and no backbone.

8. A — Return it to where you found it
   Animals should be returned to their home.

9. B — An animal with a backbone
   Vertebrates have a backbone.

10. B — Butterfly
   A butterfly has six legs and three body parts.

11. D — Earthworm
   An earthworm has a soft body and no backbone.

12. A — Lizard
   A lizard has dry scaly skin.

13. D — It reminds us to do the right things every day
   A plan helps us follow healthy habits.

14. C — Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   Follow the health worker's advice.

15. D — Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
   Fast eating and dirty food can cause stomach pain.

16. A — Oesophagus
   The gullet is also called the oesophagus.

17. C — A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   Bloating means the tummy feels full and swollen.

18. A — 250 ml
   A cup holds about 250 ml.

19. C — The air in a balloon
   Air is a mixture of gases.

20. A — To avoid spreading germs
   Sharing a balloon that has been in someone's mouth can spread germs.

21. D — 650 ml
   400 + 250 = 650 ml.

22. A — Mass
   Both are 1 kg. The feathers take up much more space.

23. C — Solid
   Each grain is a small solid.

24. C — A rake
   A rake or shovel keeps hands away from the waste.

25. B — None of the used washing water
   Used washing water is not safe to drink.

26. C — To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   A cover stops mosquitoes breeding and dirt getting in.

27. A — A gutter and a tank
   Gutters carry rain to a tank.

28. C — To keep it safe from germs
   Covered clean containers protect water.

29. A — Leaving a tap running
   A running tap that is not in use wastes water.

30. B — Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   The air has very little effect on the crumpled paper.

31. B — It makes them warm
   Friction produces heat.

32. A — A force
   The pump pushes air by force.

33. C — A rough carpet
   Rough surfaces give more friction.

34. B — The sun
   The sun is found in nature.

35. B — Wood
   Wood blocks light.

36. D — Electric bulbs
   Bulbs are artificial light.

37. C — Paraffin lamp
   A paraffin lamp is a made light source.

38. D — A cold stone in the shade
   A cold stone gives out no heat of its own.

39. D — Charcoal
   Charcoal gives out heat when it burns.

40. D — Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth
   Gloves stop heat reaching your hand.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gravity and friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use three cards with holes in the middle and line them up in a row. Shine a torch through the holes. Light passes. Move the middle card and the light is blocked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Pushing a wheelbarrow, pulling a plough, lifting water from a well with a rope, hammering a nail, kicking a ball, stitching clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Windows and translucent roof sheets (skylights).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Air or oxygen for breathing, cooking gas for cooking, air in tyres or footballs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each gas with its use.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect. It is an invertebrate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for six legs, 1 mark for eight legs, 1 mark for conclusion.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A liquid has a fixed volume and no shape of its own. It takes the shape of its container and can be poured.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of two properties and 1 mark for the example.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: chalk and book. Liquids: milk and cooking oil. Gases: oxygen and steam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch it while hot, switch off after use, keep it away from children, do not touch with wet hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric kettle, iron, cooker, heater, hair dryer, toaster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Solid (stone), liquid (water), gas (air).
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for the three states and 1 mark for correct examples.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 200 ml of water into a tall glass and then into a wide bowl. The shape of the water changes but the amount stays the same.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two containers, 1 mark for shape changing, 1 mark for the volume the same.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: A toy car from a box and bottle tops. Beads from rolled paper. A flower vase from a tin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each toy and 1 mark for each list of materials.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon into a cup of warm water. After two minutes touch the top of each. The metal feels warmer so metal passes heat easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Blocked drains and floods, disease from flies and rats, harm to animals, injuries from glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each danger.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use windows and translucent sheets by day, solar lamps and LED bulbs at night, keep candles and paraffin away from cloth, turn off lights when not needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaving taps running, leaking taps or pipes, using too much water for washing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: Heat keeps us warm, cooks food, dries clothes and crops, helps plants grow, makes rain by evaporation, and is used to make metals and glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water is taken back from the leftover food and the rest becomes faeces.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and 1 mark for faeces.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: They keep their shape so we can build houses, make tools, furniture, clothes and shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.
